Analysis.object: Self concept subdomains are indirectly related to disturbed eating attitudes and behaviors through their relations with global and physical self worth in non-elite athlete adolescent girls competing in different types of sports.

The cross sectional deisgn prevents causal interpretation and also precluded the consideration of inter-individual differences in rates of growth and maturation that may be involved in the development of disturbed eating attitudes and behaviors. We focused on a single leaness/aesthetic sport whereas research shows that elite athletes involved in some weight controlled, but not aesthetic sports, such as boxing or judo, may also present an elevated prevalence of disturbed eating attitudes and behaviors. This study was performed using a small convenience sample exclusively composed of non-elite adolescents girls of dubious generalizability.

It would be interesting to investigate similar relations in a sample of elite basketball players for whom reliance on these more extreme stretagies would likely prove counter-productive in the long term.

Population.object: French adolescent girls between the ages of 12 and 16 years
